messages.content:
You look into one unusual day in the public NYC 311 service-request data: one complaint type in one community district had far more requests than the usual for that weekday. Use the tools to look at the day, then write a short finding with submit_finding.

Tools: series (daily counts), breakdown (the day's requests split by descriptor, zip code, hour, agency, location type or status), neighbours (the same complaint type that day in other districts), weather (rain and the day's high at Central Park) and events (permitted events that list this district and whose scheduled span covers the day; a long span does not mean activity throughout it).

Rules for the finding:
- Say what the spike is associated with, using only what the tools returned. Use the words "associated with" or "coincided with". Never write any of these: "caused", "causing", "cause of", "because of", "due to", "owing to", "led to", "leads to", "leading to", "result of", "resulted in", "results in", "as a result", "triggered by". A submission containing one is refused.
- Any comparison (above, below, more, fewer, unusual, a surge, a spike) states both numbers it compares, taken from the tool results, such as "58 against about 19 usual".
- If the tools show nothing that goes with the spike, say so plainly. Do not guess.
- Two to four plain sentences, under 450 characters (a summary over 600 is refused), with the numbers you rely on.
- Every tool result begins "ref <n>:", a number. evidence lists the numbers of the tool calls the summary relies on, for example [1, 3]. You can cite only results you have already read, so call the tools first and submit in a later reply: a submission in the same reply as new tool calls cannot cite them. Set wording_check to true only after you re-read the summary for the banned words.
Every reply you send, including errors, uses up one of a small number of calls; when two remain you must submit.

Date 2026-11-24 (Tuesday). HEAT/HOT WATER in Queens community district 4: 56 requests, against about 8.5 usual for that weekday (6.6 times). You have 5 calls in all; each reply uses one. Read the tool results, then submit in a separate reply.
